purpose: Adjudicated convention-C comparison sites for scripts/convention-c-value-audit.py. An entry here is the ONLY thing that stops a confirmed convention-C binding from blocking that audit.
why_a_committed_file: The audit reads no names and no comments, by design: its whole premise is that it cannot be evaded by re-spelling, and docs/audits/2026-08-15-detector-blindness-taxonomy.md records sixteen spellings that defeated shape-matching detectors, four of them found BY detectors written to catch the previous blind spot. A '# comparison only' comment or a z_C-style name would be an exemption an author grants themselves inside the file being audited -- the same evasion surface, one level up. A ledger entry cannot be granted that way. It lives outside the scanned tree, it must be committed as a separate deliberate act, and its key includes a hash of the site's own source line, so editing that line expires the adjudication automatically. Same shape as docs/audits/lean-vacuity-review-ledger.json, which holds agent verdicts a machine cannot reach for the same reason.
what_co_binding_is_not: The audit reports which confirmed-C sites are co-bound with a convention-D binding in the same enclosing scope. That is a value-level hint at which sites are PROBABLY comparisons, and it deliberately carries no exemption power: it can be gamed by adding a throwaway z_D beside the site. Co-binding is why a site gets PROPOSED for the ledger (--propose-ledger). It is never why a site is exempt; the commit is.
how_to_add_an_entry: 2. Take the stub for the site you are adjudicating.
3. Fill in `rationale` with why that site binds z_C deliberately -- what it compares, and what would be lost by binding only z_D.
5. Commit it here. Do NOT edit the audited source to make the site disappear; that is AGENTS.md 1a audit-dodging.

6. If the site's source line later changes, the entry stops matching and the site blocks again. That is intended: the adjudication was about that expression, and it is now a different one. The audit lists such entries as `stale` (non-blocking) so they can be pruned or renewed.

entries.rationale: `z_of(q, convention)` is a two-arm frame-comparison helper: the D arm returns the canonical `markov_z(q) = q**3/(q**2+1)`, the C arm returns `sqrt(q)/(q+1)`, and the probe calls both to measure the frame difference in the He-4 body-order shortfall. The function's own docstring scopes the C arm 'excised - computed here ONLY to measure the frame difference, never wired'. Binding only z_D would delete the comparison the probe exists to make. NOTE: --propose-ledger does NOT stub this site, because its D arm is a CALL (`markov_z(q)`) rather than an inline z_D binding, so the co-binding hint does not fire. Adjudicated by hand for that reason; see bean qou-1jny.
entries.adjudicated_by: claude (session 2b6a2d13)

entries.rationale: Two-arm C-vs-D comparison whose D arm lives in LEAN, not in this file. The probe's A5 assertion checks tr_C(pi_lambda) = w_lambda(t)*d_lambda against the Markov-forced weights of the Lean `BorromeanCanonicalTraceDerivation` (`trC_borromean_derived`), which is the convention-C arm of a deliberately-maintained C/D pair; the D arm is `BorromeanMarkovTrace`, and `BorromeanTraceConventionSplit.lean` proves D != C sorry-free. So z_C here is the object under comparison, not residual C: binding z_D would make the probe compare the D value against the Lean C weights and assert a known-false equality. RESOLVES the in-file note of 2026-08-10, which feared the reverse (that the Lean side had moved to D leaving this comparison mismatched). Evidence is the probe's own exact-symbolic PASS: because D != C is a THEOREM, a mismatched pairing could not pass, so the Lean weights it cites are necessarily C. Verified by running it (A5 traces: True, 4/4 assertions).

Two-arm frame-comparison helper `z_of(q, convention)`: the D arm returns the canonical `markov_z(q) = q**3/(q**2+1)`, the C arm returns `sqrt(q)/(q+1)`, and the probe evaluates BOTH to show its 2/3 threshold verdict is convention-independent. The function's own docstring scopes the C arm: 'excised, computed here ONLY to show the threshold verdict is convention-independent'. Binding only z_D would delete the comparison the probe exists to make -- the verdict's convention-independence is the result. Instance of taxonomy ROW 17 (the D arm is a CALL to the canonical helper, not an inline re-spelling, so the co-binding test sees no D-shaped expression in scope); same shape as the already-adjudicated he4_body_order_shortfall_location_probe.z_of, which is row 17's worked example.

This IS the sanctioned named convention-C source. `markov_parameter_convention_C` exists precisely so that a deliberate C consumer is greppable rather than inlining sqrt(q)/(1+q); flagging its own return as residual C would be flagging the guard for doing its job, and migrating it to z_D would make the function a liar to every caller that asks for C by name. The registry registers this symbol under `evaluators.z` as C so R9 asserts z_C numerically on every validator run. Newly VISIBLE (not newly introduced) on 2026-08-30: the helper was mpmath-only and raised TypeError on a sympy Symbol, so symbolic consumers had to inline C and were invisible to the guard (taxonomy row 21); adding the sympy branch is what put this return in the audit's view. The mpmath arm at the same site is the identical object in the other numeric tower.

Two-arm C-vs-D comparison with BOTH arms as sibling defs in the same file: `def z_C` at :60 (docstring 'Convention C, excised 2026-08-09') and `def z_D` at :64 returning q**3/(q**2+1). The probe asks whether the q-GoL golden-ratio threshold is convention-dependent and PRINTS both values side by side ('same recipe, z_D = ...'). Binding only z_D deletes the comparison the probe exists to make. Taxonomy ROW 18 (sibling-def spelling: scope-local co-binding sees neither arm from the other).

Two-arm comparison, co-bound in one scope: zD = q**3/(q**2+1) at :133 immediately above zC at :134. The probe's conclusion is explicitly about the C arm -- :160 reports the bar-parity 'identity fails for z_C (markov_z_full_bar_condition_probe)' -- so z_C is the object under test and removing it removes the finding. The audit already tags this site [co-bound with z_D]; co-binding is reported but does not by itself exempt, hence the explicit adjudication.

NOT residual C: this probe (bean qou-3j5m) independently reconstructs THE ONLY RECORDED CONSTRUCTION, `computations/_deprecated/toffoli-braid.py`, and compares three things -- its reconstruction, the producer's committed witness, and the values published in the content blocks. All three are convention-C-era artefacts. The reconstruction matches the producer EXACTLY (symbolic zero, both diagonals), which is what establishes the recipe as the framework's; rebuilding it with z_D would compare against a construction nobody recorded and would destroy the audit's purpose, which is to locate a published-vs-construction discrepancy (3 of 4 published entries do not match). Same class as probe_h3_central_idempotents_exact: reproducing a DEFINED C-era object, not carrying residual C.

Mirrors a LEAN-DEFINED object and must track it, not be migrated independently. The script emits the witness discharging `gramMatrix_det_ne_zero`, whose Gram entries are fixed by the Lean side; `u/(u**2+1)` is the generic-u spelling of the Markov kernel, matching Lean `markovKernel (u : R) := u / (u ^ 2 + 1)` in MarkovConventionSeparation.lean. Per AGENTS.md the Tier-2 migration that replaced `Real.sqrt q` with a generic `markovZ (u : R)` DID NOT change the convention -- it removed the square root and left C harder to see -- so this is convention C in the generic-u disguise. Migrating the Python alone would DESYNCHRONISE the witness from the theorem it discharges. The Lean-side C surface is tracked separately as qou-cxjq; this site should move when that does, and not before.

`z_naive` is one of the two PARAMETER-FREE magnitudes the probe fixes BEFORE comparison under its stated anti-fit discipline (the other is g_reeb); it is the object under study, named 'naive' precisely to mark it as the unrefined candidate being tested against the derived reeb magnitude and the 1/sqrt(5) ceiling. Substituting z_D would test a different candidate and invalidate the recorded comparison. Adjacent finding recorded in the source, not migrated: the companion `z_bar_even` assertion is VACUOUS -- z_bar differs from z_naive only by commuting the addition, so the difference is exactly 0 and the assertion cannot fail. The claim is true (z is bar-even) but the symmetry is syntactic, so no formulation of that test can be non-vacuous; g_bar_even by contrast is a genuine algebraic identity check. Labelled in situ so the witness's two assertions are not read as equally strong.

The probe's entire subject is the C-vs-D selection: its docstring states the test as 'ONE equation in ONE unknown -- if it has a unique solution z_D, and the weight vector at z_D equals the Jones-closure vector, then convention D is [selected]', and :71 records the result, 'NOT a root of y_(1^3) = 0 while z_D is -- i.e. the two-row forcing selects D'. z_C is the arm being tested AGAINST and its exclusion is the finding. Binding z_D deletes the comparison that produced the corpus's own evidence for D.

One of THREE tabulated convention variants, declared as such in the source: :123 'Markov parameter -- multiple conventions; tabulate them', and the witness description at :220 records 'candidates z_M (three convention variants), and mixed'. The probe exists to tabulate the variants side by side; keeping only one defeats the tabulation.

The z of the CORPUS CLOSED FORM being cross-checked, not residual C. The probe verifies tr_M(σ₁²) = (q-q⁻¹)z + 1 against the closed form of trm-hopf-sigma1-sq-closed-form.md, which is proved over ℚ(q^{1/2}) WITH z = 1/(√q + 1/√q); it then cross-checks a second, independent q-Schur Plancherel decomposition of the same object. Measured: the quantity is NOT C/D-invariant -- z_C gives 1.1043880582592 and matches the closed form, z_D gives 1.1280887441144 and does not -- so substituting z_D would test the closed form against a value it was never proved to equal. ALSO LABELLED IN SITU: the adjacent comment 'Identical in Wenzl and q-Schur conventions at H₂' is true but is about the WENZL-vs-Q-SCHUR axis, not C-vs-D; sitting one line above this binding it reads as a convention-safety clearance it does not provide.

Explicit two-arm probe: Z_C at :45 and Z_D at :46 are ADJACENT module constants, and the source annotates Z_C itself -- 'excised, used ONLY as a second z probe point' -- against Z_D 'canonical'. The probe evaluates the phi1 separability question at both z values; keeping only Z_D removes the second probe point the test is built on.

Two-arm, co-bound one line apart at the top of main(): z_C at :103, z_D at :104. The file declares the C-frame context 7 times and carries 19 D-arm references -- it is a D-frame prune that needs the C weight to state what it is pruning against.

Inside an explicit `convention == "C"` / `elif convention == "D"` dispatch -- the function is convention-PARAMETERISED, so the C branch is its contract, not residual C. The source additionally records why the spelling is kept verbatim rather than normalised to the algebraically equal sqrt(q)/(1+q): the two differ by 1.6e-61 relative at 60 dps, and 'this is the one ladder that must not be perturbed by a substitution, however small'. Rewriting it would be a precision change disguised as a cosmetic one.

The probe's axis is h-frame vs u-frame -- 'does re-expressing the Q_beta ladder in h = q - 1/q instead of u = b*hbar_q^2 fix the anchor-instability? DECISIVE TEST, and the answer is NO' -- NOT C vs D. z_C is the single convention held fixed while that other axis is varied, and it is the frame the ladder lives in. Substituting z_D would vary two axes at once and destroy the decisive test.

Self-declared and load-bearing: the site carries '# convention C -- see docstring', and the docstring at :32 states 'NOR is this a convention-D measurement. The whole ladder is convention-C-frame'. That is the qou-cds1 caveat asserted in-file -- the c_k ladder is C-frame throughout and must be RE-DERIVED under D, which is not a z-swap (QOU.QBeta.decayLadder_zC_threeRow_ne_zero proves the C-frame ladder and the mass channel's three-row forcing are mutually exclusive). Migrating this site alone would produce a number belonging to neither frame.

Self-declared at :46-47: 'Convention C throughout (the frame the extraction is defined in). The D-frame ladder is a separate open item, qou-cds1.' The probe's subject is why two neutron masses move c_3, and c_3 is not measured but EXTRACTED by inverting the experimental Q_beta against an ansatz that labels its own row '[fit]'. That extraction is DEFINED in the C frame, so z_C is not an evaluation choice here -- it is the frame the extracted quantity exists in. Substituting z_D would invert against a different ansatz and produce a c_3 that is not the one under discussion.

Settles the 'c_3 = -2 exact' claim on the post-bug-fix compute, and the c_3 extraction it tests is C-frame BY CONSTRUCTION: the same `substrate()` helper derives z, then alpha = (z-1)*h/2 and Q_A_over_me, which `extract_ck` inverts to get c_k. The probe exists to adjudicate a claim made ABOUT the C-frame ladder (a 2026-07-06 docs commit asserting c_3 is exactly -2 for all q, and that the cross-anchor swing was a 0-indexed generator-bug artifact). Re-basing it on z_D would answer a question nobody asked and leave the recorded claim unadjudicated. Same qou-cds1 caveat: the D-frame ladder is a separate open item requiring RE-DERIVATION, not a z-swap.

z_C IS THE OBJECT OF STUDY, and this is provable rather than argued. The probe derives, symbolically in formal q, that z = sqrt(1+w)/(2+w) with w = q-1 is ALGEBRAIC hence D-finite, and exhibits its first-order ODE at :112, `(4 + 6w + 2w^2) z' + w z`. MEASURED both ways: with z_C the residual is EXACTLY 0; with z_D it is (w+1)^2 (w(w+1)((w+1)^2+1) + 2((w+1)^2+3)(w^2+3w+2)) / ((w+1)^2+1)^2, i.e. nonzero. Substituting z_D would not re-express the result, it would FALSIFY the probe's own theorem. NOTE FOR READERS: 'D-finite' in this file means differentiably finite (holonomic), NOT convention D -- a grep for 'D' here misleads.

C-frame by construction, identically to qbeta_c3_cross_anchor_exactness: z feeds `alpha = (z - 1) * hh / 2` at :74, the ladder's alpha. The probe computes the Q_beta ladder's rungs in the h frame and is the companion to QOU/QBeta/LadderFrameChange.lean. Note the Lean proves the ALGEBRA over a generic field -- that genericity is about the frame-change identity, not about the Markov convention, so it does not make this site convention-neutral. Same qou-cds1 status as the rest of the ladder: C-frame throughout, D requires RE-DERIVATION.

Q_beta ladder work: the probe realizes the archimedean evaluation map's bar-decomposition, following the B3-U obstruction, and its stated premise is that 'the c_k come from the archimedean evaluation, not a fibre basis change'. The c_k ladder is convention-C-frame throughout per qou-cds1 and has not been re-derived under D; a z-swap here would mix a D-frame Markov parameter into a C-frame c_k decomposition and produce a quantity belonging to neither.
